definitions.explanation: The natural ability to feel, maintain, or respond to rhythm, whether in music, dance, sports, or speech.

examples.english: To have a good sense of rhythm.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はリズム{感|かん}がないからダンスが{苦手|にがて}だ。
examples.english: He has no sense of rhythm, so he's bad at dancing.

examples.japanese: リズム{感|かん}を{鍛|きた}えるには、メトロノームに{合|あ}わせて{練習|れんしゅう}するのが{効果的|こうかてき}だ。
examples.english: Practicing with a metronome is effective for training your sense of rhythm.

notes:
A compound of the loanword リズム (rhythm) and {感|かん} (sense, feeling). Refers to one's innate or developed ability to perceive and reproduce rhythmic patterns.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- リズム{感|かん}がある: to have a sense of rhythm
- リズム{感|かん}がない: to have no sense of rhythm
- リズム{感|かん}を{鍛|きた}える: to train one's sense of rhythm
- リズム{感|かん}が{良|よ}い/{悪|わる}い: to have good/bad rhythm

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {音感|おんかん}: sense of pitch — the ability to distinguish musical tones
- テンポ{感|かん}: sense of tempo — specifically about speed/pace

USAGE:
The {感|かん} suffix is productive and attaches to many words to mean "sense of ~": {方向|ほうこう}{感|かん} (sense of direction), {距離|きょり}{感|かん} (sense of distance), {季節|きせつ}{感|かん} (sense of the season).
